title: Largest area between two lines
summary: Pick two fence planks as the walls of a rain barrel so it holds the most water, dropping the shorter wall each step.
goal: Choose two planks that hold the most water between them

examples.label: Nine planks
examples.explanation: Planks 1 (height 8) and 8 (height 7): water rises to 7 over a width of 7, so 49.

examples.label: Tall ends
examples.explanation: The two end planks, both 4 high and 4 apart, hold 16.

ladder.name: Try every pair of planks
ladder.idea: Measure the water between every pair of planks and keep the largest.

ladder.name: Drop the shorter wall
ladder.idea: Start with the widest barrel. Measure it, then move the shorter wall inward and measure again, keeping the best.
ladder.insight: Water only rises to the shorter wall. Every narrower barrel that keeps that wall holds less, so the shorter wall can be dropped for good.

approaches.name: Drop the shorter wall
approaches.summary: Measure the widest barrel, then always move the shorter wall inward.

transfer.problem: Two towers on a skyline: choose two buildings so that a banner hung between their roofs, sagging to the lower roof, has the largest area.
transfer.explanation: It is the same trade-off between width and the shorter of two heights: start widest and move the lower building inward.

selfCheck: Uses the shorter of the two walls for the water level.
Moves the shorter wall, not the taller one.
Keeps the best area seen, not the last one.
Stops when the two walls meet.
